<issue>
FileWatcher stop working if the FileWatcher object is collected by GC
The `FileWatcher` will stop working if the FileWatcher object is collected by GC, it should keep process running and only be cleaned up when `FW.close()` is called, just like `tjs.serve`.
```ts
// define a variable to hold a reference of FileWatcher object
const h = tjs.watch("./test.txt", () => {
	console.log("works");
})

tjs.watch("./test.txt", () => {
	console.log("disposed");
})

// Process will exit if there is only a FileWatcher is running, use a infinite promise to keep process running
await new Promise(res => {});
```


</issue>

The repository is at /testbed.

content.text:
I changed `src/mod_fswatch.c` so a watcher stays alive until `close()` is called, but I haven't built it or run any tests.

The watcher object now holds a reference to itself, the same approach `tjs.serve` uses. It also marks that reference for GC. The reference is released in the handle's close callback, which runs after `close()`. Until then the GC can't collect the object, so the watcher keeps working even if your script drops its reference.

- **Naming:** the repo has no class called `FileWatcher`. The implementation is `FsWatcher`, and that's what I edited.
- **Shutdown risk:** the close callback releases the self-reference. If libuv closes the handle during runtime teardown, that call could touch a runtime that is already being freed. I didn't check that path.

I didn't write a test for your example.
